_comment: DOCS-NAME-2: the words this product is not allowed to invent.
The rule is not 'avoid jargon': use the product's
own nouns and AZURE'S OWN TECHNICAL NAMES, and never invent a softer word
for something that already has one. Vagueness is not plain language.
This list exists because Test-SimplifiedEnglish cannot see the difference.
'The network is on the faster adapter' is short, active, and made of
common words, so the wording gate had nothing to object to - and it was on
A list of banned phrases only catches what somebody already thought of, so
this is NOT the whole answer - it is the part a test can carry. Add a row
when a sweep finds another one. Both the manual and the dashboard strings
are checked, because every word an operator reads is in scope.

avoid.why: Azure's own name - the resource is a network interface, the portal says network interface, and this manual's own reference pages and the dashboard already said it. Seven places in the narrative pages invented a synonym.
Azure's own name. The property is the disk controller type, and this manual's reference and technical pages already said disk controller.
DOCS-NAME-1. Azure names both the feature and the adapter, and the same page named the adapter correctly eleven lines above.

avoid.use: what the check or the step actually does
avoid.why: DOCS-NAME-1. 'The machine answers from the inside' named nothing. The check runs a script inside the machine and reads the disk it starts from.

avoid.use: when the product actually verifies it
avoid.why: DOCS-NAME-1. It claimed capacity was settled in advance. Quota is verified and a restricted size is named; capacity itself is only guaranteed by a reservation.

_notAvoided: 'network adapter' is NOT on this list on purpose: MANA is the Microsoft
